Canada's coastline is roughly six times the length of the equator.

01 — 243,042 km of coastline, the longest of any country. The equator is 40,075 km. (The CIA Factbook says 202,080 km. Both are "right" — coastline length depends entirely on how finely you measure, which is a genuine unsolved problem in geography called the coastline paradox.)

02 — 52,455 islands. Baffin Island on its own is bigger than Spain.

03 — 8,890 km of border with the United States, the longest international border on Earth. Second place is Russia–Kazakhstan at 6,846 km.

04 — 9,984,670 km² of land, second largest country in the world, behind Russia.

05 — And the myth: Canada does NOT have more lakes than the rest of the world combined. That one is false and it is everywhere. What's true is that Canada has more lake AREA than any country, including 563 lakes larger than 100 km². The accurate version is more impressive than the myth.

Which of these five did you already know?

Bali had its moment. Canggu is now a traffic jam with a beach attached, and Seminyak is a shopping centre. Say it.

Five beach towns that still work:

01 JERICOACOARA, Brazil — you arrive by 4WD across sand dunes. No paved roads, no street lighting, and at sunset the entire village climbs the big dune to watch.

02 TAGHAZOUT, Morocco — a fishing village that became a surf town without becoming a resort. Atlantic point breaks and tagine for the price of a flat white.

03 PAJE, Zanzibar — kitesurfing flats on a turquoise lagoon, with a tide that retreats almost to the horizon twice a day.

04 AN BANG, Vietnam — Hoi An's beach without Hoi An's crowds. Seafood shacks directly on the sand, lantern-lit old town 15 minutes up the road.

05 LAGOS, Portugal — golden cliffs and sea caves on the Algarve, in a town that still has a life in February.

Opinion, obviously. The rule we used: would you go in the off season?

Chile is roughly 4,300 km long and averages under 200 km wide. It is a country shaped like a road.

That extreme shape is the whole point of visiting. Because it covers so much latitude, you get the driest non-polar desert on Earth at the top and glaciers and fjords at the bottom, with Mediterranean wine valleys and temperate rainforest in between.

CHILE BY NUMBERS
Capital — Santiago
Area — 756,102 km²
Land borders — 3 (Argentina, Bolivia, Peru)
Official language — Spanish
Currency — Chilean peso

The Atacama is where the world's major observatories are built, because the combination of altitude, dryness and near-permanent cloudlessness is almost unmatched anywhere.

WHERE TO GO
San Pedro de Atacama — salt flats, geysers, and the clearest night sky you will ever stand under.
Torres del Paine — the W trek, five days beneath granite towers.
Carretera Austral — 1,240 km of mostly gravel road through fjords and rainforest.

Desert or Patagonia — which end of Chile are you starting at?

Iceland spent centuries as one of the only inhabited places on Earth with no mosquitoes. That ended in October 2025.

01 — Iceland was essentially mosquito-free until October 2025. What made it strange is that it shouldn't have been: Greenland has mosquitoes and it is colder. Scotland and Norway have them at similar latitudes. Iceland had the standing water, the summer and the wildlife to feed on.

02 — Only around 1,300 insect species are known in Iceland. Over a million have been described worldwide. Midges, though, are everywhere — Mývatn literally translates as "midge lake".

03 — Effectively 100% of Iceland's electricity is renewable. In 2025: 70.5% hydro, 29.4% geothermal, 0.1% fossil fuel.

04 — About 85% of ALL energy used in the country — not just electricity — comes from domestic renewable sources.

05 — 90% of Icelandic homes are heated geothermally, straight from the ground. The same system keeps Reykjavík's pavements clear of ice in winter.

A country that runs on heat from under its own feet, and has just inherited the world's most annoying insect.

Does this change whether you'd go?

Thailand is not cheap any more. It is good value, which is a different claim. Bangkok and the islands now cost real money.

Five places where a month still costs very little:

01 GEORGIA — many nationalities get a full year visa-free on arrival, which is among the most generous entry policies in the world. Tbilisi rents remain low and the food is excellent.

02 ALBANIA — Adriatic and Ionian coast at a fraction of Croatian prices, and Tirana has become genuinely interesting rather than merely cheap.

03 VIETNAM — still the best cheap food culture in Asia. Da Nang and Hoi An run far below Bangkok.

04 COLOMBIA — Medellín sits in spring weather all year, so you pay nothing to heat or cool anything.

05 TÜRKIYE — outside Istanbul's tourist core, costs fall steeply. Izmir and Antalya undercut anywhere comparable in the EU.

Check current visa rules before you book anything. Entry policies change more often than prices do, and we are not a visa service.

Which of these is already too expensive?

Georgia borders Russia, Türkiye, Armenia and Azerbaijan. Four neighbours, and no two of them alike in language, alphabet or alliance.

It sits exactly where Europe stops being Europe, and it has spent most of its history being argued over by whoever was largest at the time.

GEORGIA BY NUMBERS
Capital — Tbilisi
Area — 69,700 km²
Land borders — 4
Official language — Georgian
Currency — lari

Georgia has its own alphabet. Not a variant of Cyrillic or Latin — its own script, used essentially nowhere else, and recognised by UNESCO.

It also has an 8,000-year winemaking tradition using qvevri, large clay vessels buried in the ground. That method is itself UNESCO-listed. This is plausibly where wine was invented.

Many nationalities can stay a full year visa-free, which is among the most generous policies in the world — but check your own passport before you book, because entry rules change.

WHERE TO GO, past Tbilisi:
Svaneti — medieval stone defence towers under glaciated peaks.
Kakheti — the wine region, poured in courtyards by the people who made it.
Vardzia — a cave monastery carved thirteen levels into a cliff.

Is Georgia in Europe or Asia? Settle it in the comments.

Japan has 14,125 islands. For 35 years the official number was 6,852.

Nothing was discovered. No territory was gained. Not one square metre.

The 1987 figure came from the Japan Coast Guard, counting by hand off a paper map. That method quietly merged clusters of small islands into single entries, because at that resolution they looked like one thing.

In 2022 the Geospatial Information Authority recounted using digital mapping. The computer detected more than 100,000 separate landmasses. Only those with a circumference of 100 metres or more made the official list — the exact same threshold the 1987 survey used.

Result: 14,125.

Japan's territorial waters, its land area and its borders are all unchanged. The only thing that changed was the measuring instrument.

Makes you wonder which other numbers in the atlas are just old equipment.

What's a "fact" you learned at school that turned out to be measurement error?

Prague is not on this list. Neither is Budapest. Both were genuinely underrated once; neither has been for about twenty years.

Five European cities that still are:

01 TBILISI, Georgia — sulphur baths built into a cliff, Soviet concrete next to carved wooden balconies, and an 8,000-year wine tradition using buried clay qvevri.

02 PORTO, Portugal — steeper, cheaper and rougher than Lisbon, with azulejo tiles peeling off facades above a working river.

03 LJUBLJANA, Slovenia — a capital you can walk across in 30 minutes. Alps one way, Adriatic the other, both about two hours.

04 GDAŃSK, Poland — a Hanseatic port rebuilt brick by brick after 1945. Amber, cranes, and Westerplatte, where the Second World War started.

05 VALLETTA, Malta — a fortified limestone city on a peninsula, compact enough to feel like one neighbourhood.

This is opinion, not data. We're not pretending there's a formula.

Now tell us why we're wrong about Prague.

Mongolia borders exactly two countries. China and Russia. That is the entire list.

It is 1.56 million km² — roughly the size of Western Europe — and every road and rail line in or out passes through one of two superpowers. There is no third option. No port. No neutral neighbour.

MONGOLIA BY NUMBERS
Capital — Ulaanbaatar
Area — 1,564,110 km²
Land borders — 2
Official language — Mongolian
Currency — tögrög

It is also one of the least densely populated countries on Earth. Grassland runs to the horizon in every direction and a significant share of the population still herds livestock on horseback.

WHERE TO GO
Gorkhi-Terelj for granite formations and ger camps near the capital. The Orkhon Valley, UNESCO listed, which was the heart of the Mongol empire. The southern Gobi for the Khongoryn Els dunes and the Flaming Cliffs, where the first dinosaur eggs known to science were found.

Could you handle a week with no phone signal?

The lowest place in Lesotho is 1,400 metres above sea level.

That is higher than the summit of Ben Nevis — and it is a river junction, not a mountain.

01 — 1,400 m is the highest "lowest point" of any country on Earth. It sits where the Orange and Makhaleng rivers meet.

02 — Lesotho is the only independent state that lies entirely above 1,000 metres. There is nowhere in the country that is low.

03 — Over 80% of it sits above 1,800 metres.

04 — The high point, Thabana Ntlenyana, reaches 3,482 m. It is the highest peak in southern Africa.

05 — It has exactly one neighbour, South Africa, completely surrounding it. Only three countries in the world are enclosed by a single other state: Lesotho, San Marino and Vatican City.

Because of the altitude it snows — in southern Africa — and there is a ski field. They call it the Kingdom in the Sky, which for once is not a tourism board exaggerating.

Would you rather live somewhere with no sea level, or no mountains at all?

Paris has extraordinary restaurants and is an overrated eating city. Those are different claims and both are true.

Five where the street food outguns the fine dining:

01 GEORGE TOWN, Penang — two centuries of Chinese, Malay and Indian cooking in one small place. Char kway teow, assam laksa, nasi kandar. Probably the best street food on Earth.

02 OAXACA, Mexico — seven distinct moles, each taking a day. Markets selling chapulines, tlayudas and mezcal from the same stall.

03 ISTANBUL — where the Balkans, the Caucasus and the Levant meet and eat. Turkish breakfast is a two-hour, fourteen-plate event.

04 OSAKA — the local word kuidaore means to eat yourself into ruin. Takoyaki, okonomiyaki, kushikatsu, all at counters.

05 LIMA — Japanese, Chinese, African, Andean and Spanish traditions folded together over 150 years. Nikkei and chifa are the interesting part; ceviche is just the door.

The pattern: the best eating cities are port cities and trade crossroads. Food gets interesting where cultures were forced to share a kitchen.

Where should we have put Bangkok?

Morocco has a land border with Spain. In Africa.

Ceuta and Melilla are Spanish cities sitting on the North African mainland, entirely surrounded by Moroccan territory. They are part of the European Union. You can walk from Morocco into the EU without crossing water.

MOROCCO BY NUMBERS
Capital — Rabat (not Marrakech, and not Casablanca)
Area — 446,550 km²
Official languages — Arabic and Berber (Amazigh)
Currency — dirham

Inside one country you get Atlantic coast, Mediterranean coast, the High Atlas with snow on it, and the Sahara. Very few countries that size carry that much variety.

Fez el Bali, the old medina of Fez, is one of the largest car-free urban areas on Earth. Not a pedestrianised zone — a medieval city that cars were never able to enter.

WHERE TO GO, past Marrakech:
Chefchaouen — blue-painted town in the Rif mountains.
Taghazout — Atlantic surf village south of Agadir.
Merzouga — the Erg Chebbi dunes, where the Sahara begins in earnest.

Did you know the EU has a land border with Morocco?

Vatican City is the only country on Earth where nobody is born a citizen.

01 — The whole country is 0.44 km². It is smaller than Central Park. Monaco, the second-smallest country, is nearly five times the size.

02 — There is no hospital and no maternity ward. Nobody is born there, so nobody acquires citizenship by birth.

03 — Citizenship is granted on appointment — you get it by being given a job serving the Holy See. Cardinals, Swiss Guards, officials.

04 — When the job ends, the citizenship ends with it. Anyone who would be left stateless automatically becomes an Italian citizen instead.

05 — Around 800 people live there. Fewer than occupy a single large apartment building in most cities.

It is the only country in the world whose population is, in effect, a staff list.

Would you take a citizenship you could be fired from?

The Maldives is the most overrated island destination on Earth. You fly for a day to sit on a resort you cannot leave, on an island engineered to look like its own brochure. It is a photograph you are allowed to stand inside.

Five islands almost nobody goes to:

01 SOCOTRA, Yemen — roughly a third of its plant species exist nowhere else. The dragon's blood trees look like set design for a film about another planet.

02 SÃO TOMÉ AND PRÍNCIPE — volcanic spires wrapped in rainforest in the Gulf of Guinea, with abandoned colonial plantations and effectively no tourism industry.

03 LORD HOWE ISLAND, Australia — a hard cap of 400 visitors at any one time. UNESCO listed, two volcanic peaks, and a lagoon.

04 FLORES, Azores — waterfalls down every cliff, crater lakes on top, and four kinds of weather before lunch.

05 SVALBARD, Norway — 78°N, closer to the North Pole than to Oslo. Months of polar night, and more polar bears than people.

Some of these are hard to reach and one is genuinely difficult to enter. That is the point of the list.

Which island did we unfairly write off?

Namibia recognises nine languages, and one of them is German. That is a direct inheritance of German colonial rule, which ended over a century ago and is still legible in the street names.

NAMIBIA BY NUMBERS
Capital — Windhoek
Area — 825,615 km²
Land borders — 4 (Angola, Botswana, South Africa, Zambia)
Recognised languages — 9, including Afrikaans, German, English, Herero and Khoekhoe
Currency — Namibian dollar

It is also nearly empty. Among the lowest population densities of any country on Earth, which means roads with nobody on them for hours at a time.

The Namib is where a desert runs straight into the Atlantic. A cold current meets hot desert air and produces a dense fog — which is the only dependable water source for most living things on the Skeleton Coast. There are beetles that stand on dune crests at dawn and drink condensation off their own backs.

WHERE TO GO
Sossusvlei — red dunes and the dead camelthorn trees of Deadvlei.
Etosha — a salt pan visible from orbit, ringed with waterholes.
Fish River Canyon — one of the largest canyons anywhere, almost deserted.

Desert or ocean? Namibia refuses to choose.

Zimbabwe recognises 16 official languages. No country recognises more.

Chewa. Chibarwe. English. Kalanga. Koisan. Nambya. Ndau. Ndebele. Shangani. Shona. Sign language. Sotho. Tonga. Tswana. Venda. Xhosa.

01 — All 16 were formalised in the 2013 constitution. Zimbabwe holds the Guinness World Record for the most official languages in a single country.

02 — Zimbabwean Sign Language is one of them. Very few constitutions anywhere give a signed language equal official standing alongside spoken ones.

03 — Languages can be added to the list by an Act of Parliament. There is no mechanism to remove one.

04 — For comparison: South Africa has 11 (12 since sign language was added). India lists 22 scheduled languages but only two at union level. Most countries manage one.

05 — In practice three do the work. Shona and Ndebele are what most Zimbabweans speak. English still runs government, business and schooling — a direct inheritance of colonial rule, and the uncomfortable part of the story.

Recognising a language and resourcing it are not the same thing.

How many languages are official where you live?

Ibiza is finished. It stopped being a destination and became a venue — a place where the experience is now priced by proximity to a table.

Five cities where the night still belongs to the city:

01 BERLIN — still the reference point. Industrial spaces, stickers over your phone camera, a door policy you cannot buy your way past, and nights that end on Monday.

02 TBILISI — a club scene that grew directly out of political protest, operating inside a Soviet-era stadium. It means something there in a way it doesn't anywhere else.

03 BELGRADE — splavovi, floating clubs moored on the Danube and the Sava. In summer the whole night happens on the water.

04 MEDELLÍN — salsa and reggaeton in a city where dancing is a basic competence, not an event.

05 MEXICO CITY — mezcalerías in Roma through to warehouse parties, in a city far too big to be fully colonised by visitors.

The pattern: the best nightlife is in cities where locals outnumber visitors and the scene answers to them.

Which city would you put above Berlin?

Nepal has two neighbours: China and India. Between them they hold about a third of humanity.

Nepal sits in the gap, landlocked, 147,181 km², with the Himalaya forming its northern wall.

NEPAL BY NUMBERS
Capital — Kathmandu
Area — 147,181 km²
Land borders — 2
Official language — Nepali
Currency — Nepalese rupee

Eight of the world's ten highest mountains stand on or across its borders, Everest included. The country runs from subtropical jungle in the south to 8,000-metre peaks in the north, and the whole transition happens in about 200 kilometres.

It was also never colonised by a European power — unusual for the region, and a large part of why Nepali culture reads so differently from its neighbours'.

WHERE TO GO
Annapurna Circuit — the classic, over the Thorong La at 5,416 m.
Everest Base Camp — busy, and still extraordinary.
Chitwan — lowland jungle with rhino and tiger, which almost nobody associates with Nepal.

Mountains or jungle — which Nepal would you go for?

#nepal #himalaya #everest #annapurna #kathmandu #trekking #travelnepal #geographyfacts #travelinspo #earthbynumbers

Route 66 is the most overrated drive on Earth. Large parts of it no longer exist as a continuous road, and much of what remains is a frontage road running past closed motels selling nostalgia for itself.

Five that earn the hire car:

01 CARRETERA AUSTRAL, Chile — 1,240 km of largely gravel road through Patagonian fjords, glaciers and temperate rainforest. Ferries are part of the route, not a detour.

02 PAMIR HIGHWAY, Tajikistan — the second-highest international highway in the world, over passes above 4,600 m, through the Wakhan Corridor with Afghanistan on the far bank.

03 GARDEN ROUTE, South Africa — coast, mountain passes and forest, with wildlife as an optional extra.

04 RING ROAD, Iceland — 1,332 km around an entire country, and the weather will try every one of its options on you.

05 WEST COAST, New Zealand — glaciers, rainforest and the Tasman Sea, on a road with almost no one else on it.

The rule: a great drive needs the landscape to change. Distance alone is just commuting.

What's the best road you've ever driven?

Peru has three official languages: Spanish, Quechua and Aymara. Two of them predate the Spanish by a long way.

Quechua was the administrative language of the Inca empire and is still spoken by millions of people today. It is not a heritage project — it is official, and it is alive.

PERU BY NUMBERS
Capital — Lima
Area — 1,285,216 km²
Land borders — 5 (Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador)
Official languages — Spanish, Quechua, Aymara
Currency — sol

Geographically it is three countries stacked together: a desert coastline, the high Andes, and Amazon rainforest. You can go from sea-level desert to 4,000 m to jungle without leaving the country.

The history is deeper than most people realise. Caral on the coast is among the oldest known urban sites in the Americas — thousands of years before the Inca, who are comparatively recent.

WHERE TO GO, past Machu Picchu:
Arequipa — white volcanic-stone city under three volcanoes, next to the Colca Canyon.
Huascarán — glaciated peaks and turquoise lakes in the Cordillera Blanca.
The northern coast — Chan Chan's adobe ruins and Moche pyramids, almost empty.

Could you name Peru's five neighbours?

#peru #machupicchu #arequipa #quechua #andes #amazon #travelperu #geographyfacts #travelinspo #earthbynumbers

Iceland is a bad stargazing destination. It is cloudy, it is wet, and for months of the year it barely gets dark. People go for the aurora and come back having seen weather.

Five skies that actually deliver:

01 ATACAMA DESERT, Chile — the driest non-polar desert on Earth, at altitude, almost permanently cloudless. There is a reason the world's major observatories are built here rather than anywhere else.

02 AORAKI MACKENZIE, New Zealand — an International Dark Sky Reserve where outdoor lighting is restricted by law. The southern sky, the Magellanic Clouds, and almost no haze.

03 NAMIBRAND, Namibia — a private reserve in the Namib with essentially no light pollution for hundreds of kilometres.

04 LA PALMA, Canary Islands — observatories sit at 2,400 m, above the cloud layer. A sky-protection law has restricted light pollution since 1988.

05 JASPER, Canada — one of the largest accessible dark sky preserves anywhere, and you get aurora on top.

The rule: altitude, dryness, and a local government that regulates lighting. Pretty scenery is irrelevant if the air is wet.

Where did you see the best night sky of your life?

Portugal has exactly one land neighbour, and that border has barely shifted in seven centuries.

It is one of the oldest continuously defined frontiers in Europe — substantially settled since the late 1200s, while almost every other border on the continent was redrawn repeatedly by war.

PORTUGAL BY NUMBERS
Capital — Lisbon
Area — 92,090 km²
Land borders — 1 (Spain)
Official language — Portuguese
Currency — euro

That single border is the whole story of the place. With Spain to the east and nothing but Atlantic to the west, Portugal went outward by sea instead — which is why Portuguese is an official language on four continents.

WHERE TO GO, past Lisbon:
Porto — steeper, rougher, cheaper, on a working river.
Alentejo — cork oaks, wheat, whitewashed hill towns, almost no visitors.
Azores — nine volcanic islands in the middle of the Atlantic.

Lisbon or Porto? Pick one and defend it.

#portugal #lisbon #porto #azores #alentejo #traveleurope #geographyfacts #travelinspo #worldfacts #earthbynumbers

Pipeline isn't on this list. It's the most photographed wave in the world and it still isn't top five.

01 NAZARÉ, Portugal — the Nazaré Canyon is about 5 km deep and runs almost to the shoreline, funnelling and amplifying Atlantic swell into the biggest rideable waves ever recorded. This is the one genuinely measurable entry here.

02 TEAHUPO'O, Tahiti — not the tallest, the heaviest. It breaks over shallow reef and the lip carries a frankly unreasonable volume of water.

03 JEFFREYS BAY, South Africa — a right-hand point break that simply keeps going. The shape argument ends here for a lot of people.

04 ULUWATU, Bali — reef break beneath a clifftop temple, accessed through a cave you time against the sets.

05 RAGLAN, New Zealand — one of the longest left-hand point breaks anywhere. You measure the ride in minutes, not seconds.

Ranking waves is opinion. The canyon is the only part you can put a number on.

Go on then — defend Pipeline.

#surf #surfing #nazare #teahupoo #jeffreysbay #uluwatu #raglan #surftravel #waves #traveltheworld #earthbynumbers

Slovenia is 20,273 km² and contains the Alps, the Mediterranean, the Pannonian plain and classic karst country. You can ski in the morning and swim in the Adriatic in the afternoon, and people actually do it.

SLOVENIA BY NUMBERS
Capital — Ljubljana
Area — 20,273 km²
Land borders — 4 (Austria, Italy, Hungary, Croatia)
Official language — Slovene
Currency — euro

Those four neighbours are the whole character of the place: Alpine, Mediterranean, Pannonian and Balkan influences meeting in a country smaller than Wales.

More than half of it is forest, among the highest proportions in Europe. And the word "karst" — used worldwide for limestone cave landscapes — is named after the Kras region here. This is the type specimen.

WHERE TO GO, past Lake Bled:
Soča Valley — a river an unreasonable shade of turquoise, running through a First World War front line.
Škocjan Caves — an underground canyon with a river at the bottom, UNESCO listed.
Piran — a Venetian-era town on a thumb of land poking into the Adriatic.

Smallest country you've visited that surprised you most?

The Orient Express is a very good hotel that happens to move. It is not a great train journey. You are paying to look at the dining car.

Five where the window is the point:

01 TRANS-SIBERIAN, Moscow–Vladivostok — roughly 9,300 km, about seven days, eight time zones. The longest continuous rail service on Earth.

02 QINGHAI–TIBET, Xining–Lhasa — over the Tanggula Pass above 5,000 m. The carriages are pressurised and pipe in supplementary oxygen, because without it people struggle.

03 BELGRADE TO BAR — 435 km, 254 tunnels, 435 bridges, mountains to the Adriatic in one day. Probably the best value scenic rail journey in Europe by a distance.

04 BERGEN LINE, Oslo–Bergen — about seven hours across the Hardangervidda plateau.

05 TRANZALPINE, Christchurch–Greymouth — across the Southern Alps in under five hours.

A flight deletes the distance. A train makes you feel it. That's the whole argument.

Which one would you actually book?

Vietnam is about 1,650 km from top to bottom and narrows to roughly 50 km at its waist. The shape explains almost everything about the place.

Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City are around 1,100 km apart, with different climates, different accents and genuinely different food. Treating Vietnam as a single destination is the standard mistake.

VIETNAM BY NUMBERS
Capital — Hanoi
Area — 331,212 km²
Land borders — 3 (China, Laos, Cambodia)
Official language — Vietnamese
Currency — đồng

Northern pho is clear, restrained, herb-light. Southern pho is sweeter, cloudier, piled with herbs and sprouts. People hold firm views. Both are correct.

WHERE TO GO, past Ha Long Bay:
Ha Giang Loop — limestone mountains on the Chinese border, by motorbike over three or four days. Probably the best thing in the country.
Phong Nha — cave country, including some of the largest cave passages on Earth.
An Bang — Hoi An's beach without Hoi An's crowds.

North or south — which Vietnam is better? Choose carefully.

Bolivia maintains a navy of roughly 5,000 personnel. Bolivia has no coastline.

It lost the coast in 1879, when Chile occupied the port of Antofagasta without resistance and took the Litoral province with it. Bolivia signed a truce in 1884 and has been landlocked ever since. The navy was not disbanded. It was reorganised, and it is still there.

BOLIVIA BY NUMBERS
Naval personnel — about 5,000 (2018)
Coastline — 0 km
Land area — 1,098,581 km²
Land neighbours — 5: Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina, Chile, Peru
Lake Titicaca — 3,812 m above sea level, 8,372 km²

The fleet patrols Lake Titicaca and thousands of miles of navigable river running into the Amazon basin. Wikipedia puts the purpose plainly: the navy exists to keep alive the hope of recovering the coast.

Two other things worth knowing. Bolivia has two capitals — Sucre is the constitutional capital and holds the judiciary, La Paz is the seat of government. And since independence the country has lost more than half its territory to its neighbours.

One correction, because it gets repeated everywhere: Titicaca is not the highest lake on Earth. It is the highest navigable lake, and that claim is generally understood to mean commercial boats. The crater lake on Ojos del Salado sits above 6,400 m. Titicaca is still the largest lake in South America, by surface area and by volume, which is impressive enough without the upgrade.

France's longest land border is not with Spain or Germany. It is with Brazil.

730 km of it, along French Guiana. The Spanish border is 646 km. Nothing in metropolitan France comes close.

FRANCE BY NUMBERS
Longest land border — 730 km, with Brazil
Second — 646 km, with Spain
French Guiana — 83,534 km², slightly smaller than Austria
Time zones — 12, more than any other country on Earth
Range — UTC−10 to UTC+12

French Guiana is not a colony or a territory. It is an overseas department and region of France, which means it is part of the European Union. The euro is legal tender in South America. The European Union has a land border with Brazil.

It is also why Europe launches its rockets from the Amazon. The Guiana Space Centre at Kourou sits about 5 degrees north of the equator, and the closer you are to the equator the less energy it takes to put something into geostationary orbit. ESA owns the launch infrastructure. Europe's spaceport is in South America, and that is a deliberate choice about physics, not history.

Twelve time zones is the part people argue about. It runs from UTC−10 in French Polynesia to UTC+12 in Wallis and Futuna — thirteen if you count the Antarctic claim.

The lowest point on land in Africa is a lake, and it is saltier than the Dead Sea.

Lake Assal sits 155 metres below sea level in Djibouti. At the surface it measures 276.5 grams of salt per litre. The Dead Sea measures 268.8.

Finland has 187,888 lakes. It also has 5,600 lakes. It also has 309 lakes. All three numbers are correct.

187,888 counts everything larger than 500 square metres — five ares, roughly a large garden. Move the threshold to 0.1 km² and 97% of them disappear, leaving about 5,600. Move it to 10 km² and you are left with 309.

FINLAND BY NUMBERS
Capital — Helsinki
Land area — 338,424 km²
Land borders — 3: Sweden, Norway, Russia
Official languages — Finnish and Swedish
Currency — euro

None of those numbers is wrong and none of them is the truth. They are three answers to three different questions, and the only reason 187,888 is the famous one is that it is the biggest.

Wikipedia says so itself, in a line most people scroll past: there is no standard unambiguous definition of the size requirements for a body of water to be classified as a lake. Every lake count you have ever seen — for Canada, for Minnesota, for anywhere — is a threshold someone picked.

The largest of them, Saimaa, is the fourth-largest natural freshwater lake in Europe.

This is the thing about superlatives. Somebody chose the units.

05 SATURNIA, Italy — the Cascate del Mulino. Free, open all night, limestone bowls with 37 °C water pouring through.

Every single one of Madagascar's 651 terrestrial snail species is found nowhere else on Earth. Not most. All of them.

That is what 88 million years alone does to a place. Madagascar separated from Africa around 180 million years ago and from India about 88 million years ago, and everything living on it has been evolving in a sealed room ever since.

MADAGASCAR BY NUMBERS
Capital — Antananarivo
Land area — 587,041 km²
Land borders — none. It is the world's fourth-largest island
Official languages — Malagasy and French
Currency — ariary

Roughly 90% of all plant and animal species on the island are endemic. Reptiles run above 90% across more than 260 species. Plants are lower but still extraordinary: more than 80% of 14,883 species grow nowhere else. Some ecologists call the island the eighth continent, and the label is not really an exaggeration.

Now the part that is less fun. As of 2012 there were 103 recognised species and subspecies of lemur, and a 2012 assessment found 90% of lemur species threatened with extinction. At least 17 species have already gone, since humans arrived.

An island that spent 88 million years building something unrepeatable can lose it in a couple of centuries. Those two numbers belong in the same post.
